Method of Attack: Utilizes SSH credentials found on compromised systems to propagate across networks
Self-modification and size reduction during initial execution by removing comments, redundant functions, and whitespace
Hunts for private keys in various locations, including shell history files and common directories
Parses shell history files to identify commands referencing SSH private keys
Analyzes system logs and network cache to pinpoint potential targets and gather information for private key discovery
Impacted Systems: Enterprise environments using SSH for secure connections
Attack Vector: Lateral movement by leveraging SSH keys for propagation
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of self-modifying bash shell script
Unusual parsing of shell history files (e.g., .bash_history, .zsh_history)
Network mapping and dependency analysis targeting SSH vulnerabilities
